## Why this study was run

**Research question:** [When do promising signals fail?](../questions/failure-conditions.qmd); [Can model responses provide useful ranking evidence?](../questions/response-evidence.qmd)

Test whether source-query alignment should precede target-response evidence.

**Rationale:** The frozen protocol, result receipt, and decision receipt define the test.

## Protocol and comparison

**Hypothesis:** Selecting aligned sources first improves response-derived candidate ranking.

Construct source-alignment variants and evaluate only the explicitly frozen comparable systems.

Any run comparison below is partitioned by ledger evaluation scope.

## Current result

**Outcome:** `negative`

The evaluated source-alignment systems did not beat the established control; three constructed variants remain unscored.

## Decision and rationale

**Decision:** `stop`

Stop this path in its current form and retain unscored constructions as non-results.

Rationale provenance: `contemporaneous`.

## Evidence limits

Development-only; constructed-not-evaluated systems have no effectiveness values.

Development results do not establish hidden-test effectiveness.
